AGENDA
  PLANNING COMMISSION

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to
the Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to
a vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or
service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  MAY 14, 2025

The meeting was called to order by Vice Chair Apodaca at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City
Hall, Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-Salas, and Vice Chair Apodaca.
Commissioner Barragan and Chair Lopez were absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton,
Interim Director of Community Development; Araceli Almazan, Deputy City Attorney;
Matthew Morales, Planning Intern; Kristy Wong, Associate Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann,
Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of April 23, 2025.

DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST (DAR) NO. 2025-04
Robert Drieslein on behalf of Norwalk Taco Factory (“Applicant”); a request to permit the
sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption (Type 41 ABC license) in an existing 1,400
square foot bona fide restaurant within an approximately 1.39-acre commercial shopping
center. The subject property is generally known as 12227 Norwalk Boulevard located
within Paddison Square on the southwest corner of Norwalk Boulevard and Crewe Street
(also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8024-024-023) in the General
Commercial (C-3) Zone.
Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).

Vice Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Matthew Morales, Planning
Intern, presented a report stating that the applicant is requesting approval to allow the
sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption (Type 41 ABC license) in an existing 1,400
square foot restaurant (Norwalk Taco Factory) within an approximately 1.39-acre
commercial shopping center (Paddison Square); that the subject site is considered a high-
crime reporting district, however, the City’s Public Safety Department has issued
conditions of approval to address this concern; that the alcohol service will be ancillary to
the existing bona fide restaurant; that the conditions of approval include the following:
ending beer and wine sales 60 minutes before closing; providing a video surveillance
system; and conduct responsible beverage server and Department of Beverage Control
licensee training for employees. Further, he added that the project is consistent with the
General Plan vision of providing adequate local-serving commercial uses; that it is exempt
from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301
(Existing Facilities), and that it is staff’s recommendation that the Commission approve
the applicant’s request subject to the conditions of approval.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  May 14, 2025

The applicant, Robert Drieslein, stated that he acquired the Taco Factory about a year
ago; that it was a challenge as the restaurant had changed hands many times; that his
concept for the restaurant was to provide fresh food at great prices in a family friendly
environment; that they went from serving about three hundred meals a day to almost two
thousand meals a day; that they are offering dollar tacos on Tuesdays; that he also owns
Kung Pao, a Chinese bistro restaurant in Norwalk which has been in existence for about
thirty years; that he sees this city as his second home; and that he thanks the Commission
for their consideration.

Vice Chair Apodaca commented on the floor plan which shows the proposed location of
the beer cooler adjacent to a bathroom. She stated that she has a concern with customers
walking by the cooler on their way to the bathroom, and she asked if there is another
location for the cooler.

Andre Gulmesoff, Business Consultant, stated that, in the beginning, they were going
back and forth on where to place the cooler; that they considered various alternatives, but
none of them worked; that they could put a lock on the cooler, and that they would agree
to any recommendations made by the Commission.

In response to Commissioner Vernola-Salas’ question whether it is correct that the
customers can get their own sodas from the self-serve soda machine, Mr. Gulmesoff
answered in the affirmative, and he added that they are doing the best they can with the
space that they have.

Jennifer stated that she oversees everything in the restaurants owned by Mr. Drieslein;
that she wants to add that the restaurant is a sit-down establishment; that when customers
come in it is highly unlikely that they would grab anything as they are being seated by
staff; that the cooler is in staff’s line-of-sight and is never unattended; and that they have
no problem with keeping it locked. Further, she shared that they are adamant in
constantly training all of their employees.

Commissioner Macias indicated that his concerns have been answered.

Since there were no other persons wishing to testify, Vice Chair Apodaca closed the
public hearing.

Commissioner Macias stated that should the applicant encounter any problems, he is
sure that they would be able to address those.

Commissioner Vernola-Salas shared that adding beer and wine to the menu is a great
idea; that she is a bit concerned with access to the cooler, but that she agrees with the
recommendation that a locking device be added; and she welcomed the applicant to
Norwalk.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  May 14, 2025

Vice Chair Apodaca stated that the restaurant is a welcome addition to the shopping
center; that they want to make all businesses economically viable; and that she is in
support of the request with the added condition of making the cooler more secure.

It was moved by Commissioner Macias and seconded by Vice-Chair Apodaca to: (1)
adopt Resolution No. 25-07 to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2025-04
subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”, and that a condition be
added that the storage area for beer and wine shall be secured with a lock, carabiner, or
any other similar devices to prevent direct customer access; and (2) consider and find
that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-Salas, and Vice Chair
  Apodaca.
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Barragan, and Chair Lopez

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development, shared that staff will be
attending the International Council of Shopping Centers (ICSC) conference next week in
Las Vegas. He stated that staff have two full days of meetings with hotel developers,
brokers and potential restaurant businesses; and that he will report back to the
Commission on the results.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 6:26 p.m.

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development

BY:  Carlos Rojas, Senior Planner

SUBJECT:  HEART OF NORWALK SPECIFIC PLAN UPDATE

Recommendation:

Staff recommends the Planning Commission receive and file the Draft Heart of Norwalk Draft
Specific Plan presentation from The Arroyo Group and provide feedback.
Introduction/background:

On July 6, 2021, the City Council adopted The Heart of Norwalk Vision Plan for the future of San
Antonio Village and the Firestone Corridor, two key neighborhoods in the center of the City. The
Plan was developed in partnership with the City, the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) and the consulting firm, The Arroyo Group (TAG). This Vision Plan sets the
overall tone for how the study area can grow in both the commercial and housing sectors, while
balancing place making and open spaces. The Vision Plan emphasizes providing new commercial
amenities, open spaces, complete streets, and affordable housing to support Norwalk residents. In
order to implement this vision, Planning staff worked with TAG to initiate the drafting of a Specific
Plan that would establish zoning regulations and development standards to make this vision into
reality.
Project Description:

The proposed Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan (“Specific Plan”) effort intends to establish zoning
regulations that will allow housing and desired commercial uses while ensuring that each
development contributes to community goals. It will also establish a program of street, open space,
and infrastructure projects to support the vision of the plan and future growth. The Specific Plan
also outlines funding sources and implementation measures.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  June 25, 2025
Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan Update  Page No. 2

The Specific Plan area contains a wide variety of commercial and residential zoning districts. Staff
notes that currently within the commercially zoned properties, housing is permitted in conjunction
with a commercial development (i.e. mixed use) with an approved Conditional Use Permit. It is
estimated that these commercial sites could reasonably be developed with 2,053 residential units
under current zoning regulations. The Specific Plan is intended to be implemented over a 30-year
period.
Additionally, the development of the Specific Plan will help the City in meeting its 2021-2029
Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) of 5,034 units. The current Housing Element accounted
for many of the sites within the Heart of Norwalk area as residential inventory sites available for
development. Therefore, the Housing Element contains a program that commits to adopting the
Specific Plan, which would allow residential use.
Community Feedback
The project team has received robust and consistent input for the project since the beginning of the
Vision Plan process in fall 2020. The Vision Plan outreach campaign engaged approximately 5,300
residents between December 2020 and March 2021. Nearly 100 residents attended four online
events that were held in February and March 2021, 363 surveys were completed by community
members, and over 3,000 residents engaged with Heart of Norwalk social media content.
Outreach in the Specific Plan process consisted of virtual and in-person community workshops and
participation at three Front Street events in the summer of 2022 and in the summer of 2024. Further
community workshops and social media engagement will take place prior to the Specific Plan being
considered by Planning Commission and City Council for adoption.
Throughout the outreach process, members of the public have consistently expressed the desire
for high-quality local commercial options, places to enjoy in groups and spend time in public. They
desire an authentic center to the City, with local and national businesses, places to walk and spend
time, nightlife, and spaces that can encourage and celebrate local culture, such as performance arts
spaces.
Front Street, a focal area for businesses and nightlife, retains its historic feel by preserving older
buildings. It caters to the community’s younger population. Norwalk Town Square, on the other
hand, offers shopping, family entertainment, and convenient parking. Multifamily residential uses
are also supported, as they contribute to the desired commercial amenities. Public surveys and
workshops revealed a desire to connect these districts through streets, prioritizing walking, biking
and public space over traffic movement.
On February 20, 2024, a Study Session was conducted with City Council to provide an update of
the Specific Plan and gather feedback from City Council and the public.
Specific Plan Progress
The project team circulated the Draft Environmental Impact Report (EIR) on June 23, 2025, for a
45-day public review period ending on August 7, 2025. Concurrently, the draft Specific Plan is also
available for public review for the same duration. Although not required, Planning staff and TAG
plan to conduct outreach meetings with property owners within the Specific Plan area during July
and August 2025. These meetings aim to provide property owners with a refresher on the Specific
Plan and address any concerns. The City will continue to receive public feedback and additional

input regarding the proposed land use plan to finalize the Specific Plan’s zoning regulations and
Draft  EIR.  The  documents  can  be  found  using  the  following  link:
https://www.norwalk.org/departments_services/community_development/heart_of_norwalk.php
Next Steps
Once the review period concludes, Planning staff and TAG will commence preparing the associated
Response to Comments (RTC) for the Draft EIR and incorporate any final modifications to the
Specific Plan. Staff anticipates scheduling the Specific Plan and the EIR for consideration to the
Planning Commission in October 2025, and it is expected for consideration before the City Council
in November 2025.
